sourceContext: R36 bounded local crash recovery: canonical pre/post proof, disposable candidate rebuild, attempt-scoped candidate-bound journals and fresh Hotel data-state certification.
objective: Complete truthful final local schema and Hotel data-state certification with PostgreSQL catalog-generated type fragments, server parse preflight, dependency-aware reconciliation, independent reviewers and real rollback recreation for release 698c.
why: R36 prevents stale failed journals from poisoning rebuilt disposable candidates and recovers only from exact canonical pre/post state; Production remains unreachable.
scope: Apply ordered schema and ACL effects with data-state exclusions
acceptanceCriteria: Target reference build is persisted and resolves release artifacts exactly once
Every distinct release-managed target formatted_type passes local PostgreSQL parse preflight with zero unsupported types
Fresh candidate contract equals immutable baseline before mutation
Dependency-aware actions record exact preconditions, postconditions, reads, writes and dependencies with no unresolved overlapping writes
Independent RLS, RPC, storage, grant, constraint, migration and dependency reviewers have P0=0, P1=0, P2=0 and P3=0
Existing unsafe column type transitions fail closed and no valid catalog type is reconstructed or mapped to text
Candidate destroy and restore from the same verified backup equals baseline with no residue
Canonical Hotel DATA_STATE_PATCH effect hash is verified and executed only on a separate disposable local restore with bounded-change, audit and rollback evidence
Production reads and mutations remain zero
Post-DDL candidate ACL closure converges to target in at most two bounded passes, including PostgreSQL default PUBLIC EXECUTE grants created by structural DDL.
ACL closure actions have separate durable package, journal and result evidence with exact GRANT/REVOKE postconditions.
Hotel data-state prepatch query uses public.properties with exact property id, display_code and client_id preconditions
Only the canonical DATA_STATE_PATCH effect is executed; schema APPLY effects are never replayed in data-state certification
The target candidate reaches schema and ACL convergence before the data-state patch
Audit content verifies correction action, property identity, previous client, new client and display code
Full-row hashes for bounded unrelated relations remain unchanged
Schema and ACL rollback recreation both pass with durable domain, reviewer, rollback and data-state evidence
Crash recovery uses three-state canonical pre/post semantics for structural and ACL actions
A local ambiguous candidate is destroyed and recreated from the same verified backup with a new attempt-scoped journal
Journal validity binds runId, candidateInstanceId, attemptNumber, backupSha256 and packageHash
Maximum candidate rebuild budget is two and repeated recovery fingerprints fail closed
Fresh baseline, target and candidate instances are used for this certification
forbiddenActions: change Production RLS, grants, RPCs or schema
execute unbound or ad-hoc data patch
verificationRequirements: Record lifecycle journal without secrets or paths
Verify baseline immutability before and after extraction
Verify target artifacts resolve exactly once
Verify backup hash immediately before restore
Prove rollback recreation and zero residue
Record PG catalog formatted_type source, type hashes and parse-preflight result
Verify default collation normalization and explicit collation preservation
